model: Specialty P&C insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

inputs.total_debt_note: Senior notes and other debt ~$1,831M + subordinated debentures ~$1,013M (10-K balance sheet; companyfacts carries no debt-carrying-amount tag for WRB). No issuance in 2025 (ProceedsFromIssuanceOfLongTermDebt 0, repayments $2.1M), so carried unchanged. Interest expense $126.9M FY2025 ($63.4M H1-2026) is consistent with ~$2.8bn at ~4.5%. Informational only: held at zero in the bridge.
inputs.cash_note: Reported cash & equivalents $2,606.5M at 2026-06-30 is part of the ~$30bn investment portfolio backing $23.2bn of loss reserves -- operating float, not surplus cash. Held at zero.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 FCFE = capital actually distributed to shareholders: dividends paid incl. specials $700.3M + repurchases $270.2M. NOT reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income: an insurer's operating cash flow includes reserve build on float and is not free to equity. Book value ex-AOCI still grew ~$0.8bn after these distributions (retention for ~6% premium growth plus excess-capital build).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 operating cash flow (no capex tag in XBRL since FY2019; PP&E capex immaterial). Not free cash: includes growth in loss reserves funded by float.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement ShareBasedCompensation $54.5M (XBRL); H1-2026 $29.0M. RSU-based; no separate equity-award withholding figure tagged.
inputs.dividends_note: FY2025 PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock $700.3M ($1.85/share paid incl. special dividends); WRB returns excess capital through recurring special dividends rather than raising the regular $0.09 quarterly.
inputs.share_count_basis: 371,227,529 common shares outstanding at 2026-07-27 (Q2-2026 10-Q cover, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) + 17.38M vested/deferred restricted stock units WRB includes in BASIC weighted shares (WeightedAverageNumberOfSharesRestrictedStock) + ~2.65M further dilutive units (Q2-2026 diluted 391.80M less basic 389.16M) = 391.3M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is charged in the flows and repurchases are a use of the FCFE, so shrinking the count as well would double-count. The Metrics.csv SharesOutstanding column is the diluted weighted average (391.8M Q2-2026), consistent with this basis; split-adjusted for the 3:2 splits of 2019, 2022 and 2024.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 9.0% in USD: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.8 (WRB's observed beta is ~0.6-0.7; lifted for long-tail casualty reserve risk and cycle exposure not captured in a low market beta), rounded to the 9.0% used for GL/IAG.AX/PRU. It is a cost of EQUITY because the flow is post-interest FCFE (holdco interest $126.9M sits inside the pre-tax margin). Same rate in all three scenarios; risk is carried in the margin paths and weights, not stacked into the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases immaterial for an insurer; no lease adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Ignored as immaterial: NCI equity $9.8M at 2026-06-30, NCI share of FY2025 net income $5.4M (0.3%).
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO. Holdco debt (~$2.84bn) is serviced inside the flows; deducting it after capitalising a post-interest stream would count it twice. The investment portfolio and loss reserves are operating items of an insurer, not net cash or net debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a specialty P&C insurer, run through the owner-FCF component engine with net debt at zero -- the GL / PRU / IAG.AX insurer precedent. Routing-table default for insurers is BVPS compounding x exit P/B; FCFE chosen for consistency with the repo's other insurers and because GAAP book is distorted by a -$640M AOCI mark that moves with rates and by WRB's habit of paying out excess capital as special dividends, so book does not compound cleanly. A residual-income cross-check on book is given in valuation_philosophy. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenues EXCLUDING net investment gains/losses (FY2025 $14,707.9M less $132.2M gains = $14,575.6M: net premiums earned $12,446.9M + net investment income $1,429.1M + non-insurance/other ~$700M). ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income ex investment gains, BEFORE stock compensation, as % of that revenue (FY2025 ($2,280.5 - 132.2 + 54.5)/14,575.6 = 15.1%, a year with $111M Q1 wildfire cats and $44M adverse reserve development; H1-2026 ($1,191.3 + 71.0 + 29.0)/7,477.5 = 17.3%, light cats and a record 88.1% AY ex-cat combined ratio in Q2). sbc_pct_path charges SBC (~0.37% of revenue). da_pct_path = 0. capex_pct_path = statutory/rating-agency capital RETAINED to support premium growth: equity ex-AOCI is ~0.68x revenue, so retention ~0.68 x that year's growth, falling to ~2% of revenue at 3% terminal growth (no retention in the bear's flat years). cash_tax_rate_path starts near the cash rate (taxes paid $407M = 17.8% of FY2025 pre-tax; H1-2026 $205.4M = 17.2%) and ramps to the ~21.5% book rate (FY2025 495.8/2,280.5 = 21.7%), not perpetuating the timing benefit. Year-1 FCFE in base (~$1.71bn, ~85% of projected net income) sits well above the FY2025 $970M actually distributed because FY2026 earnings run ~10% higher and premium growth has slowed to ~2-3%, so little capital is needed for growth -- the gap is capital the model treats as distributable whether WRB pays it out or banks it as excess (the 2025 retention of ~$0.8bn ex-AOCI was well above the ~$0.6bn growth needed) (H1-2026 NPW +1.8%, NPE +3.1% y/y), freeing capital -- consistent with H1-2026 buybacks of $414M already exceeding all of FY2025.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR 27.4% (FY2020 COVID-trough base, diluted EPS recomputed as NI / diluted shares on a consistent post-split basis: FY2020 $1.33, FY2022 $3.49, FY2025 $4.46) and revenue 5yr 12.7% both diverge >30% from equity 5yr 9.0%. Equity understates retained earnings because WRB pays out excess capital via special dividends and AOCI swung from +$0.5bn (FY2020) to -$1.26bn (FY2022) to -$0.45bn (FY2025). The hard-market 2020-2024 growth is not a forward rate: H1-2026 net premiums written grew only 1.8% y/y.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs left null: OCF less capex is not FCFE for an insurer (OCF includes reserve growth on float). OCF CAGRs shown for reference only. EPS column in Metrics.csv mixes split bases (3:2 splits 2019, 2022, 2024); EPS CAGRs recomputed from net income / diluted shares.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands near the H1 run-rate (pre-tax margin ex gains 16.8%) with premium growth ~3% as WRB walks away from softening property, workers' comp and professional-liability pricing. The soft phase then grinds the underwriting margin down ~2pp over five years (AY ex-cat combined ratio from 88% toward ~91-92%, social inflation in casualty), partly cushioned by net investment income on a repricing ~$30bn portfolio, settling at 14.5% -- an ROE of ~16% on book ex-AOCI, between the 2010s ~10-12% and the 2023-26 ~20%. Growth re-accelerates to 5.5% when the cycle hardens mid-horizon, then fades to 3%. Terminal min(Gordon 9%/3% = 17.2x, 15x FCFE); with ~85% of terminal earnings distributable, 15x FCFE is ~13x earnings, below WRB's ~15-17x historical P/E as befits a mid-cycle exit.

bull.narrative: The decentralised unit model keeps finding rate-adequate niches (Berkley Edge, Embedded Solutions, Meridian, international), E&S share gains continue and the MSI partnership adds distribution, so premium growth runs 6-7% through the middle years; the AY ex-cat combined ratio holds in the high-80s and new-money yields lift NII, keeping the pre-tax margin at 16.5-17% (ROE ~19-20% sustained). Terminal growth 3.5%, cap 17x FCFE (~15x earnings).

bear.narrative: Social inflation forces a casualty reserve strengthening on accident years 2019-2024 in FY2027-28 while specialty rates turn negative and capacity floods E&S; WRB shrinks premium to defend margin and a rate cut lowers new-money yields, so the pre-tax margin troughs at 11% and recovers only to 12% (ROE ~13%, the 2010s norm). Shrinkage releases capital, so retention falls to zero in the flat years. Terminal growth 2.5%, cap 12x FCFE (~10.5x earnings).

scenario_narratives.base: A disciplined specialty underwriter enters the soft phase of the P&C cycle from a peak: FY2026 ROE ~20% fades to ~16% over five years as rate adequacy erodes against casualty loss trend, cushioned by rising investment income; premium growth bottoms at ~3% and recovers when the cycle turns.
scenario_narratives.bull: WRB repeats its 2019-2024 playbook of out-growing the market through new specialty units while holding a high-80s combined ratio; ROE stays near 19-20% and premium compounds 6-7%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The soft market and social inflation coincide: a reserve charge and negative specialty rates push the pre-tax margin to 11%, premium shrinks for two years, and the business settles at its 2010s ~13% ROE.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the bull-leaning house default: WRB is valued at a cyclical margin peak (record AY ex-cat combined ratio, ROE ~20%) with premium growth already decelerating to ~2% and management flagging rate deceleration in several lines, so the reserve/soft-market tail deserves as much weight as the share-gain upside. Balance-sheet risk is low (debt/equity ~0.29x, conservative reserving record), which keeps the bear from being heavier.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a specialty P&C insurer as the cash its holding company can distribute (FCFE) after retaining the capital premium growth requires, discounted at a 9% cost of equity with net debt at zero. The key judgment is the through-cycle underwriting margin: WRB's 2023-26 returns (~20% ROE) are a hard-market peak, and the base fades them to ~16%. Residual-income cross-check: diluted BVPS $25.13 (equity $9,833M / 391.3M at 2026-06-30, after a -$640M AOCI mark); at a sustainable 16% ROE, 4% book growth and a 9% cost of equity, justified P/B = (16-4)/(9-4) = 2.4x = ~$60; at 20% ROE = 3.2x = ~$80; at 13% ROE = 1.8x = ~$45.
key_risks_to_valuation: Casualty reserve adequacy: social inflation on accident years 2019-2023 ($44M adverse development in 2025) could become a material charge that resets book and the margin path
Soft-market depth: rates already declining in property, workers' comp and professional liability; a broad E&S softening would push the margin toward the bear path
Interest rates: lower new-money yields cut net investment income (~10% of revenue, a larger share of pre-tax profit) while higher rates widen the AOCI mark on book
Catastrophe volatility: H1-2026 cats were light ($76M Q1 vs $111M Q1-2025); year-1 margin assumes a normal H2
Mitsui Sumitomo's completed 15% open-market stake build was a source of buying demand that has now ended; its governance provisions also limit takeover optionality
